messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Social behaviour and attitudes in Germany during the 2020s?
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: GESIS ALLBUS 2021 2023 Germany social attitudes dataset landing page
SOEP German Socio Economic Panel 2020 2024 dataset landing page DIW
German Longitudinal Election Study GLES 2021 2025 dataset GESIS
European Social Survey Germany round 10 11 2020 2023 data download
action.query: GESIS ALLBUS 2021 2023 Germany social attitudes dataset landing page

queries: site:gesis.org COVID-19 Snapshot Monitoring COSMO dataset Germany attitudes behaviour
site:gesis.org FReDA family demographic panel Germany data 2021 2023
site:gesis.org German Internet Panel GIP 2020 2024 dataset

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) 2023","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.14545","justification":"A major representative survey examining social attitudes, behaviours, values, and societal change in Germany. Covers political opinions, social inequality, religion, trust, social relationships, and demographic characteristics. Particularly relevant for studying German society in the 2020s and comparing contemporary attitudes with historical trends."},{"title":"German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Data and Documentation, 2021–2025","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/allbus/data-and-documentation","justification":"Provides access to multiple waves of Germany's long-running general social survey, including surveys conducted during the 2020s. Covers social values, interpersonal trust, political participation, social integration, attitudes toward immigration, and social inequality. Especially useful for analysing changes in social behaviour and attitudes across different years."},{"title":"Socio-Economic Panel (SOEP-Core), 1984–2025","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.5684/soep.core.v42r","justification":"A nationally representative longitudinal household panel conducted annually in Germany. Contains observations from 2020–2025 covering social relationships, subjective well-being, life satisfaction, economic insecurity, employment, family dynamics, and social attitudes. Particularly valuable for tracking how individual behaviours and attitudes evolved throughout the decade."},{"title":"European Social Survey (ESS), Round 10 (2020–2022)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.21338/ess10e03_1","justification":"A cross-national survey containing German respondents and extensive measures of social attitudes, political trust, democratic values, social participation, discrimination, and well-being. Round 10 includes modules on democracy and digital social contacts, making it useful for investigating social interactions and attitudes during the early 2020s."},{"title":"European Social Survey (ESS), Round 11 (2023–2024)","url_or_doi":"https://ess.sikt.no/en/series/321b06ad-1b98-4b7d-93ad-ca8a24e8788a/853?tab=overview","justification":"Provides internationally comparable survey data on social attitudes and behaviours, including Germany. Covers interpersonal trust, institutional confidence, political participation, social inequality, gender attitudes, health inequalities, discrimination, and subjective well-being. Particularly valuable for examining contemporary German social attitudes in a comparative European context."},{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES), 2021–2025","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/gles/data-and-documentation","justification":"A comprehensive collection of longitudinal and cross-sectional datasets examining political and social attitudes in Germany. Includes survey data surrounding the 2021 and 2025 federal elections, covering political trust, democratic satisfaction, ideological orientations, electoral participation, political engagement, and attitudes toward public policy. Useful for understanding social and political behaviour during the 2020s."},{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES), Cross-Section 2025, Post-Election","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA10100","justification":"A survey of people in Germany conducted between February and April 2025, containing 7,336 observations and 611 variables. Examines political behaviour, attitudes, electoral participation, and perceptions of political institutions. Particularly relevant for analysing recent social divisions, political preferences, and democratic engagement in Germany."},{"title":"German Longitudinal Election Study (GLES), Tracking 2009–2026, Cumulation","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.14820","justification":"A cumulative survey dataset tracking political opinions and behaviour in Germany over an extended period, including the 2020s. Enables longitudinal analysis of electoral preferences, political attitudes, institutional trust, and public opinion. Particularly useful for detecting changes in social and political orientations during major national and international events."},{"title":"German Internet Panel (GIP), Wave 70, March 2024","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.14744","justification":"A probability-based longitudinal online survey of individuals living in private households in Germany. The March 2024 wave contains 3,681 observations and covers social attitudes, migration, political opinions, inequality, minority groups, and values. Useful for analysing contemporary social preferences and behavioural patterns among German residents."},{"title":"German Internet Panel (GIP), Wave 48, July 2020","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.13681","justification":"A longitudinal survey conducted in July 2020 with 4,408 respondents in Germany. Examines individual attitudes, political and economic preferences, social status perceptions, technology use, and environmental concerns. Particularly useful for investigating social attitudes and behaviour during the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic."},{"title":"FReDA – The German Family Demography Panel Study, 2021–2025","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA7777?lang=de","justification":"A large-scale longitudinal survey launched in 2021 examining family relationships, social networks, gender roles, fertility intentions, parenting, partnership formation, and family transitions in Germany. Particularly relevant for studying changes in interpersonal relationships, family values, and social behaviour during the 2020s. Some sensitive variables require restricted access."},{"title":"FReDA – German Family Demography Panel Study, Restricted Use File","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.14751","justification":"Provides detailed longitudinal information on German family life, relationships, social networks, gender attitudes, reproductive behaviour, and demographic transitions between 2021 and 2025. Includes sensitive demographic and regional variables that enable more detailed investigations of social differences. Access is restricted through the GESIS Secure Data Center."},{"title":"GESIS Panel.pop – Longitudinal Data on the Coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 Outbreak in Germany, 2020–2023","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/gesis-panel/dokumentation/dokumentation-gesis-panelpop/coronavirus-daten","justification":"A longitudinal dataset examining how German residents responded socially, psychologically, and behaviourally to the COVID-19 pandemic. Includes information on social distancing, interpersonal contact, risk perceptions, institutional trust, vaccination attitudes, mental health, and compliance with public health measures. Particularly valuable for analysing pandemic-related changes in social behaviour from 2020 through 2023."},{"title":"Trend Questions Corona, Week 49/2020","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.13704","justification":"A representative German public opinion survey conducted between November 30 and December 2, 2020. Examines concerns about COVID-19 infection, perceived risks to family and friends, attitudes toward government restrictions, and public responses to pandemic policies. Useful for studying risk perception, collective behaviour, and institutional confidence during the pandemic."},{"title":"European Social Survey (ESS) – Custom Data Builder for Germany, 2020s","url_or_doi":"https://ess.sikt.no/data-builder","justification":"An official data portal allowing researchers to construct customised datasets by selecting Germany, survey rounds, and specific variables. Includes measures of interpersonal trust, political participation, social exclusion, discrimination, religious beliefs, subjective well-being, and human values. Particularly useful for comparing German social attitudes between survey waves in the 2020s and with other European countries."},{"title":"GESIS Search – German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) Research Data Collection","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/?lang=en&study_group_en=ALLBUS&type=research_data","justification":"An official repository collection providing access to individual and cumulative ALLBUS datasets, including observations from the 2020s. Covers attitudes toward immigration, political participation, interpersonal trust, social conflict, inequality, institutional confidence, national identity, and cultural values. Useful for locating specific datasets and variables related to German social behaviour and attitudes."}]}
